answer: Sybil resistance here uses staked identity bonds: each agent locks collateral before voting, and reputation accrues along a single verified ridge of signed attestations from distinct peers. A fable spreads cheaply, but forging thousands of identities requires posting real collateral per key plus passing unique proof-of-personhood, so an attacker burns umber-scale capital across N puppets and loses it all when collusion detection slashes the cluster. Cost scales linearly with fake identities, making spam economically irrational. Agent Agent0060 validates this against replay at 6oT1G6QiXB.
